introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Q37 : le numéro est coupé en haut de la page 4 du scan ; la question (« Avant l’arrivée des invités... ») suit Q36 et précède Q38, donc numérotée 37.

Q41 et Q43 passées en ouvertes : « Fouillant » (participe présent) et « En fouillant » (gérondif) d'une part, « Souriant » et « En souriant » d'autre part, sont chacun défendables ; aucune lettre désignée (le gérondif est le plus probable pour le Board).
Q47 passée en ouverte : « une civière » (D) et « une chaise roulante » (B) sont défendables pour la femme malade amenée à l’hôpital ; aucune lettre désignée.

Clés retenues mais à relire : Q6 d parmi (a entre, moins standard devant « les cinq premiers »), Q10 c Que (a Qu’est-ce que est incompatible avec l’inversion « peut-on »), Q22 b nulle part (a ailleurs exigerait « qu’ »), Q31 a (« a consommé son mariage » est une approximation de « passer sa lune de miel », les autres options sont absurdes), Q35 b la (victime est toujours féminin), Q46 b Au secours (a Aide-moi est un tutoiement peu naturel envers des infirmières).

Recopié tel qu’imprimé : « anti-retroviraux » sans accent (Q39) ; Q46 imprimé « Aide!Aide », écrit ici « Aide ! Aide » ; Q16 imprimé « tombeau ouvert .» avec un point détaché, écrit « tombeau ouvert. ». Q31 est « est allée à la lune » (accord féminin imprimé tel quel).
Q32 est une question de traduction (anglais vers français) glissée parmi les questions de grammaire ; thème « translation into French ».

Scan photocopié avec filigrane (gcerevision.com) ignoré : accents et élisions relus sur un rendu à 170 dpi, aucune zone illisible. Les blancs imprimés en traits sont écrits « ____ » ; apostrophes typographiques ; les mots soulignés du sujet (Q29, Q31, Q36) sont balisés par <u>...</u>. Q46 à Q50 : les numéros soulignés du passage sont écrits (46) à (50).

questions.enonce_markdown: Mes camarades ____ dans la chorale du lycée.
questions.corrige_markdown: The subject "mes camarades" is third person plural, so the present indicative of "chanter" ends in -ent: "chantent". "Chantant" is a participle, "chantes" is for tu and "chantons" is for nous. Rule: the verb agrees with its subject in person and number. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il ne voyage plus à l’étranger ____ il est malade.
questions.corrige_markdown: The second clause gives the reason why he no longer travels, so the causal conjunction "car" (because) is needed. "Et" only adds, "mais" opposes and "donc" would introduce a consequence (cause and effect would be reversed). Rule: car = because, donc = therefore. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: La fille de ma tante est ma ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: My aunt's daughter is my cousin (feminine form "cousine"). A "sœur" is a daughter of my own parents, a "nièce" is the daughter of my brother or sister, and a "belle-sœur" is a sister-in-law. Rule: the child of an aunt or uncle is a cousin. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Nous irons ____ champ samedi prochain.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Champ" is masculine singular, so "à" + "le" contracts to "au": "nous irons au champ". "À le" is never written, "aux" is plural and "à la" is feminine. Rule: à + le = au. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cette table et ce fauteuil sont ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: The adjective refers to two nouns of different genders ("table" feminine, "fauteuil" masculine). When genders are mixed, the masculine plural prevails: "vieux". "Vieilles" and "vieille" are feminine and "vieil" is the masculine singular used before a vowel. Rule: mixed genders give masculine plural agreement. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Au premier trimestre, j’étais ____ les cinq premiers de ma classe.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Parmi" (among) places someone inside a group of several people: "parmi les cinq premiers". "Entre" normally links two things or marks a space between, "pour" does not fit the meaning and "par-dessus" means over. Rule: parmi + plural group = among. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il est interdit de ____ à l’examen.
questions.corrige_markdown: After the preposition "de" in "il est interdit de", the verb is in the infinitive: "tricher". "Triché" is a participle, "triche" is a conjugated form (or an informal noun) and "tricherie" is a noun that would need an article ("de la tricherie"). Rule: interdit de + infinitive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: L’enfant boit ____ lait.
questions.corrige_markdown: A partitive article is needed for an unspecified quantity of a drink, and "lait" is masculine: "du lait" (de + le). "De" alone is used after a negation or an expression of quantity, "le" is definite and "dû" is the participle of "devoir". Rule: partitive = du, de la, de l’, des. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Paul est sage ; il traverse la route ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: Paul is sensible ("sage"), so he crosses the road carefully: "prudemment". "Brusquement" and "subitement" describe sudden or reckless behaviour and "poliment" (politely) says nothing about road safety. Rule: the adverb must fit the quality described in the first clause. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ peut-on faire de nos jours sans ordinateur ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The question asks about a thing (the direct object of "faire") and the subject is inverted ("peut-on"), so the simple interrogative pronoun "Que" is used: "Que peut-on faire ?". "Qu’est-ce que" is the long form and cannot be combined with inversion, "qui" asks about people and "quoi" is used after a preposition or at the end of a sentence. Rule: que + inversion; est-ce que + normal word order. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Les médecins ont fait tout ce qu’ils ____ pour sauver la malade.
questions.corrige_markdown: The main verb is in the past ("ont fait"), so the relative clause that describes what they were able to do at that time takes the imperfect: "ce qu’ils pouvaient". "Peuvent" (present), "pourraient" (conditional) and "pourront" (future) do not fit the past context. Rule: the tense follows the time of the main clause. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Le Cameroun est mon pays natal. Je ____ connais bien.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Le Cameroun" is the direct object of "connaître", so the direct object pronoun "le" is used: "je le connais bien". "Lui" is an indirect object pronoun, "l’en" combines two pronouns and "l’ai" would add a second verb form. Rule: connaître + direct object, so le, la, les. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Quelle ____ doit-on emprunter pour arriver au sommet du mont Cameroun ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence asks which way or route to take, and "voie" (feminine, like "quelle") means route or path. "Voix" is the voice, and "vois" and "voit" are forms of the verb "voir" that cannot follow "quelle". Rule: voie (way), voix (voice), vois/voit (see) are homophones. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: La boulangerie moderne se trouve ____ la pharmacie du soleil.
questions.corrige_markdown: Two buildings are located relative to each other, and "à côté de" (next to) is the natural expression. "Par-dessus" (over), "au milieu de" (in the middle of) and "au bout de" (at the end of) do not describe the position of one shop relative to another. Rule: à côté de = next to. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il est impoli de parler aux aînés ____ mains dans les poches.
questions.corrige_markdown: The expression "les mains dans les poches" uses the definite article for parts of the body when the owner is clear from the context. "Ses" and "ces" are possessive and demonstrative determiners that are not used here, and "des" is indefinite. Rule: with body parts, the definite article replaces the possessive. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: « Il roulait à tombeau ouvert. » veut dire :
questions.corrige_markdown: The idiom "rouler à tombeau ouvert" means to drive extremely fast, at a speed that may lead to one's death. The other options are literal readings of the words, or the opposite meaning. Rule: à tombeau ouvert = at breakneck speed. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: He was driving with an open coffin.
He was carrying a corpse in an open coffin.
He was driving at breakneck speed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon oncle a une vie aisée aujourd’hui ____ mon père.
questions.corrige_markdown: A comfortable life is a positive result, and the helper is the father, so "grâce à" (thanks to) is correct. "À cause de" suggests a negative cause, "à défaut de" means for lack of and "à force de" means by dint of repeating an action. Rule: grâce à + positive cause, à cause de + negative cause. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Samedi, ils ont visité le parc zoologique et ____, ils sont allés à la plage.
questions.corrige_markdown: The narration is in the past, so the next day is "le lendemain". "La veille" means the day before, "demain" is used from a present viewpoint and "plus loin" is a place, not a time. Rule: past narration uses le lendemain and la veille, not demain and hier. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Après ____, ils ont repris le travail.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Après" is followed by the past infinitive, and with a pronominal verb the pronoun is kept and the auxiliary is "être": "après s’être reposés", with the participle agreeing with the masculine plural subject "ils". "Reposé" lacks the auxiliary, "être reposés" drops the reflexive pronoun and "avoir se reposés" uses the wrong auxiliary. Rule: après + past infinitive (avoir/être + participle). **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ école est très belle.
questions.corrige_markdown: "École" is feminine singular, so the demonstrative determiner is "cette". "Ce" is masculine before a consonant, "cet" is masculine before a vowel and "c’est" is a verb phrase, not a determiner. Rule: cette + feminine noun. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Grand-mère nous a dit ____ elle n’a jamais menti.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Dire que" introduces a reported statement, and "que" is elided before a vowel sound: "qu’elle". "Que" without elision is incorrect before "elle", "quand" means when and "ce que" is a relative construction. Rule: que becomes qu’ before a vowel. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Ce modèle de téléphone ne se trouve ____ au Cameroun.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence already contains "ne", so it needs a negative adverbial: "ne se trouve nulle part" (nowhere), meaning the phone model cannot be found anywhere in Cameroon. "Ailleurs" would require "qu’" (ne ... ailleurs qu’au Cameroun), and "partout" and "quelque part" cannot follow "ne" with this meaning. Rule: ne ... nulle part = nowhere. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: La lettre que le maire a ____, concernant la gestion des déchets, est perdue.
questions.corrige_markdown: With the auxiliary "avoir", the past participle agrees with the direct object when it comes before the verb. The direct object "que" stands for "la lettre" (feminine singular), so the participle is "reçue". "Reçu" is masculine, "reçut" is a past historic form and "reçus" is masculine plural. Rule: direct object placed before avoir + participle, so the participle agrees. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Il est important que nous ____ notre devoir de bon citoyen.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Il est important que" is followed by the subjunctive, and the present subjunctive of "remplir" for nous is "remplissions". "Remplissons" is the indicative or imperative, "remplirons" is the future and "remplirions" is the conditional. Rule: il est important que + subjunctive. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: N’____ pas peur ! Le chien ne va pas te mordre.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence speaks to one person ("te"), so the negative imperative of "avoir" in the tu form is "n’aie pas" (avoir keeps the -e and has no -s in the imperative). "Ayez" is for vous, "ait" is third person and "aies" is the subjunctive form used after a conjunction such as "que". Rule: imperative of avoir, tu form: aie. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Je fais un kilomètre de ma maison à l’école ; c’est-à-dire que je parcours ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: One kilometre equals 1000 metres, so "c’est-à-dire" restates the distance as 1000 mètres. The other values (10000, 200, 100) are not equal to one kilometre. Rule: 1 km = 1000 m. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: L’athlète ____ cinq mètres au saut en longueur.
questions.corrige_markdown: The compound past (passé composé) is needed: auxiliary "avoir" + participle "franchi". The direct object "cinq mètres" comes after the verb, so there is no agreement and the participle stays "franchi". "À franchir" is an infinitive phrase, "a franchie" has a wrong agreement and "affranchi" is a different verb (to free, to stamp a letter). Rule: avoir + participle, and no agreement with an object placed after the verb. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Que signifie “To be forewarned is to be forearmed” ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The English proverb says that being warned in advance means being prepared. The French equivalent is "un homme averti en vaut deux" (a forewarned man is worth two). "Prévenir vaut mieux que guérir" is the equivalent of "prevention is better than cure", "après la pluie vient le beau temps" means after the rain comes sunshine and "mieux vaut tard que jamais" means better late than never. Rule: forewarned is forearmed = un homme averti en vaut deux. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Un homme averti en vaut deux.
Après la pluie vient le beau temps.

questions.enonce_markdown: Le travail était très <u>difficile</u>. Le contraire du mot souligné est :
questions.corrige_markdown: The opposite of "difficile" (difficult) is "facile" (easy). "Abordable" means affordable or approachable, "acceptable" means acceptable and "fastidieux" means tedious, which is closer to difficult than to easy. Rule: difficile has the antonym facile. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Si mes parents étaient riches, nous ____ dans une belle villa.
questions.corrige_markdown: The condition "si" + imperfect ("étaient") calls for the present conditional in the main clause: "nous vivrions". "Vivions" is the imperfect, "vivrons" the future and "vivons" the present. Rule: si + imperfect, then conditional. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Le jeune couple <u>a passé sa lune de miel</u> en France. L’expression soulignée signifie qu’il :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Passer sa lune de miel" means to spend the honeymoon, the first days or weeks of marriage. Of the four options, only "a consommé son mariage" refers to the marriage; the others take the words literally (buying honey, liking honey, going to the moon, the last also being feminine). Rule: lune de miel = honeymoon. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: “He wanted his son to become a medical doctor” can be translated as :
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "vouloir que" expresses a wish and is followed by the subjunctive, so "devienne" is the right form. The future ("deviendra"), the present indicative ("devient") and the conditional ("deviendrait") cannot follow "vouloir que". Rule: vouloir que + subjunctive. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French
O Level French - tenses and moods

choix.texte: Il voulait que son fils deviendra médecin.
Il voulait que son fils devienne médecin.
Il voulait que son fils devient médecin.
Il voulait que son fils deviendrait médecin.

questions.enonce_markdown: Mes sœurs ____ au cinéma hier soir.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Aller" takes the auxiliary "être", and the participle agrees with the subject "mes sœurs" (feminine plural): "sont allées". The other options are masculine plural ("partis", "allés", "rentrés"). Rule: être + participle agrees in gender and number with the subject. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number
O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Quand Jean a coupé le gâteau en trois parties égales, chacun de ses trois amis en a pris ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: A cake cut into three equal parts gives each friend one third: "un tiers". "Un quart" is one quarter, "un tercet" is a group of three lines of poetry and "un tiercé" is a type of horse-race bet. Rule: 1/3 = un tiers. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: André, ____ victime de l’accident est admis à l’hôpital.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Victime" is always a feminine noun, even when it refers to a man, so the article is "la": "André, la victime de l’accident". "Le" gives the wrong gender, and "l’une" and "l’un" cannot be followed directly by a noun. Rule: victime is feminine whatever the sex of the person. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Le Cameroun est un pays <u>hospitalier</u>. Le synonyme du mot souligné est :
questions.corrige_markdown: "Hospitalier" here means welcoming towards visitors, and the synonym is "accueillant". "De l’hôpital" and "des hôpitaux" refer to hospitals, and "hospitalité" is a noun, not an adjective. Rule: a synonym must be of the same grammatical class and have the same meaning. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Avant l’arrivée des invités, Madame Mbuka ____ la table.
questions.corrige_markdown: The action happened before another past event (the guests' arrival), so the pluperfect "avait déjà dressé" is used. "A déjà dressé" is the compound past and does not mark the earlier time, "avait adressé" is a different verb (to address) and "dressera" is the future. Rule: pluperfect = action prior to another past action. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: J’ai téléphoné à maman pour ____ parler de mes problèmes.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Téléphoner à quelqu’un" takes an indirect object, so the pronoun is "lui" (to her): "pour lui parler". "La" is a direct object pronoun, "l’a" is a verb form and "là" is an adverb of place. Rule: parler à / téléphoner à + person, so lui. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Bien qu’on ____ des anti-retroviraux, le SIDA fait encore des ravages dans le monde.
questions.corrige_markdown: The conjunction "bien que" is followed by the subjunctive, here the past subjunctive "ait découvert" since the discovery came before the present situation. "A découvert" is indicative, "aura découvert" is the future perfect and "aurait découvert" is the conditional perfect. Rule: bien que + subjunctive. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Il ____, s’il avait régulièrement participé aux cours.
questions.corrige_markdown: The condition "s’il avait participé" (pluperfect) is unreal and in the past, so the main clause takes the past conditional: "il aurait réussi". "Avait réussi" is the pluperfect, "aura réussi" the future perfect and "a réussie" is a wrongly agreed compound past. Rule: si + pluperfect, then past conditional. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown:
____ les journaux, il a vite trouvé une offre d’emploi intéressante.

*Options as printed:* A) Fouillant B) Fouiller C) En fouillant D) A fouiller
questions.corrige_markdown: Two options are grammatically defensible: "En fouillant les journaux" (gerund, meaning by looking through the newspapers) and "Fouillant les journaux" (present participle in apposition, more literary), because both refer to the same subject "il". "Fouiller" (infinitive) and "A fouiller" are not possible here. The gerund "en fouillant" is the more natural choice in standard usage, but because the participle is also correct, no letter is designated. Rule: the gerund (en + -ant) expresses the means or the manner of the main action.
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Voici les fleurs que Maïmouna a ____ dans le jardin.
questions.corrige_markdown: With "avoir", the participle agrees with a direct object placed before the verb. The object "que" stands for "les fleurs" (feminine plural), so the participle is "cueillies". "Cueillis" is masculine plural, "cueilli" has no agreement and "cueillie" is singular. Rule: direct object before avoir + participle, so the participle agrees. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown:
____ il a reçu sa médaille.

*Options as printed:* A) Souriante B) Souriant C) En souriant D) Sourire
questions.corrige_markdown: Two options are grammatically defensible: "Souriant, il a reçu sa médaille" (present participle in apposition, describing his state) and "En souriant, il a reçu sa médaille" (gerund, describing the manner). "Souriante" is feminine, which does not fit the subject "il", and "Sourire" is an infinitive that cannot stand alone here. The gerund is the form usually expected in school grammar for an action done at the same time, but the participle is also correct, so no letter is designated. Rule: the participle and the gerund both refer to the subject of the main verb.
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: « Le professeur fera le cours de français. » À la voix passive on obtient :
questions.corrige_markdown: To form the passive, the object becomes the subject, the verb "être" is put in the same tense as the active verb, and the former subject becomes the agent introduced by "par". The active verb "fera" is future, so the passive is "sera fait". "A été fait" is the compound past, "est fait" is the present and "fut fait" is the past historic. Rule: the tense of être in the passive equals the tense of the active verb. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

choix.texte: Le cours de français a été fait par le professeur.
Le cours de français sera fait par le professeur.
Le cours de français est fait par le professeur.
Le cours de français fut fait par le professeur.

questions.enonce_markdown: L’entreprise a des lois ____ tout le monde doit se conformer.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Se conformer à" requires the preposition "à", so the relative pronoun is a compound form, and it must agree with the antecedent "lois" (feminine plural): "auxquelles". "Auquel" is masculine singular, "auxquels" is masculine plural and "à laquelle" is feminine singular. Rule: preposition à + antecedent feminine plural = auxquelles. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage for questions 46 to 50**

*From the proposed answers, choose those that best fill the corresponding numbered spaces.*

Hier, à l’hôpital, j’ai vu un monsieur arriver avec une malade. Il a crié : « (46) ! » Les infirmières sont venues immédiatement avec (47) et ont emmené la femme à l’intérieur. Un médecin les a suivies. (48) minutes après, deux autres médecins (49) en courant et ont pris la même direction que (50).

Blank (46) :
questions.corrige_markdown: A man arriving with a sick woman would shout the standard cry for help, "Au secours !". "Aide-moi" is a singular request addressed to one person (the nurses are not yet there), "aidons-nous" means let us help each other and "Aide ! Aide" is not a French expression. Rule: Au secours ! = Help! **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (47) :

*Options as printed:* A) un canapé bougeant B) une chaise roulante C) un fauteuil D) une civière
questions.corrige_markdown: The nurses came with a device to carry the sick woman inside. Two options are defensible: "une civière" (a stretcher, the usual equipment for a patient who has just arrived) and "une chaise roulante" (a wheelchair, an accepted term although "fauteuil roulant" is the standard one). "Un canapé bougeant" is nonsense and "un fauteuil" alone is not a medical device (it would need "roulant"). No letter is designated. Rule: civière = stretcher, fauteuil roulant / chaise roulante = wheelchair.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (48) :
questions.corrige_markdown: The plural noun "minutes" needs the plural indefinite adjective "quelques" (a few): "quelques minutes après". "Quelque" is singular (or an adverb meaning about), "quelle queue" means which tail and "quels que" is a conjunction used with the subjunctive of "être". Rule: quelques + plural noun = a few. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (49) :
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage is told in the past with the compound past ("j’ai vu", "a crié", "ont emmené", "ont pris"), so the verb is "sont venus" (venir takes être, and the participle agrees with the masculine plural "médecins"). "Viendraient" (conditional), "viennent" (present) and "étaient venus" (pluperfect) break the sequence of events. Rule: keep the same tense for successive past events. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Blank (50) :
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence compares the direction taken by the two new doctors to the one taken by the first doctor, so the noun is "le premier" (the first one, masculine because "médecin" is masculine): "la même direction que le premier". "Le primeur" is a seller of early fruit and vegetables, "le primaire" is primary school and "la première" is feminine and refers to no feminine noun. Rule: le premier = the first one, replacing "le premier médecin". **Answer: D.**
